clue.text: Support British to the maximum, dismissing Unionist? It could be decisive

indicators.note: to dismiss is to send away, so the abbreviation for Unionist is thrown out of the phrase

blocks.note: to second a motion is to support it
going all out means giving maximum effort

explanation.surface: A political question: would backing Britain to the hilt, minus the Unionists, swing the outcome?
explanation.walkthrough: Remove U from ALL OUT to leave ALLOT.
explanation.definitionFit: When a first round of voting gives no majority, a run-off vote settles the result, so it may be decisive.

clue.text: Singular set of shops, of little consequence

explanation.surface: A lone parade of shops that hardly matters to anyone.
explanation.definitionFit: Something small is minor or unimportant, the same idea as having little consequence.

clue.text: City's first matches, under review, involving one set of questions

indicators.note: first asks for only the opening letter of the word City
something under review is being reworked and reconsidered, so its letters get rearranged
to involve is to wrap something up inside, so the single digit goes within the rearranged letters

explanation.surface: A football club's opening fixtures are scrutinised, prompting a list of questions.
explanation.walkthrough: C is followed by MATCHES rearranged as ATECHSM, with I inserted to make ATECH-I-SM.
explanation.definitionFit: A catechism is a formal series of questions and answers, originally used for religious instruction.

clue.text: Fastidious about hospital specialisation?

indicators.note: about here means surrounding, so one word wraps around the hospital abbreviation

blocks.note: nice in its older sense of finely discriminating, precise

explanation.surface: Is being fussy a sign of medical specialism?
explanation.walkthrough: H goes inside NICE. Nice in the sense of fussy or precise is older than the modern 'pleasant'.
explanation.definitionFit: A niche is a specialised area or market segment, one particular field that someone concentrates on.

clue.text: Dominant child imprisoning son twice

indicators.note: imprisoning means locking inside, so the child word holds the doubled letters

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for son, taken two times

explanation.surface: A controlling youngster keeps his brother locked up, twice over.
explanation.definitionFit: A bossy person is domineering, always telling others what to do.

clue.text: Type of magazine story about spirited student I ignored

indicators.note: ignored means passed over, so the letter for I is left out of the word for spirited
about means going round, so the story word surrounds the other pieces

blocks.note: a story can be a falsehood
L for learner, a student driver

explanation.surface: A magazine runs a piece about a lively student, but leaves the writer out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Story' looks like a feature article, but it is a fib; L for student comes from the learner plate on a novice driver's car.
explanation.definitionFit: Lifestyle magazines cover fashion, homes, food and travel, a recognised genre of periodical.

clue.text: Bad language about writer's upset medical practitioner

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means turned upside down, so the possessive is read backwards
about means around, so the swearing word goes around the turned piece

blocks.note: an oath is a swear word
a poet is a writer, with the 's attached

explanation.surface: A writer is upset by swearing directed at a doctor.
explanation.walkthrough: The writer's apostrophe-s stays attached, giving the S that the reversed piece needs.
explanation.definitionFit: An osteopath treats the body by manipulating bones and muscles, a kind of healthcare practitioner.

clue.text: Deferring onset of intelligence implies responsibility

indicators.note: deferring the onset means pushing the opening letter later in the word, which reorders its letters

blocks.note: nous is common sense or intelligence

explanation.surface: Putting off the dawn of understanding suggests a duty.
explanation.walkthrough: Move the N of NOUS back one place.
explanation.definitionFit: An onus is a burden or duty that falls on someone, much like a responsibility.

clue.text: Ultimate proviso when entering farm building is blunt

indicators.note: entering means going inside, so the first pieces go into the building word

blocks.note: ult. is an abbreviation of ultimo or ultimate

explanation.surface: A final condition about entering a barn seems rather dull.
explanation.definitionFit: To stultify is to dull or deaden the mind, making it blunt in the sense of less keen.

clue.text: Gypsy dodging extravagant caper

indicators.note: dodging means avoiding, so the Gypsy word is kept out of the longer word

blocks.note: a Rom is a Romany person
romantic in the sense of fanciful or wildly imaginative

explanation.surface: A traveller ducks out of a wild prank.
explanation.definitionFit: An antic is a playful or absurd act, the same sense as a caper or prank.

clue.text: Security measure fixed, containing iron, beside river

indicators.note: containing means holding inside, so the word for fixed wraps the other pieces

blocks.note: sat in the sense of settled or positioned firmly

explanation.surface: Steel gates fixed by the riverbank to keep the site secure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fixed' is read as SAT, as in a thing that sat firmly in place; the Tyne is the river through Newcastle.
explanation.definitionFit: A safety net is a backstop or protective provision, literally the net under trapeze artists.

clue.text: Lecturer, jolly, repeated character coming to the fore being lewdness

indicators.text: repeated character coming to the fore
indicators.note: the letter that appears twice in the jolly word moves to its front, reordering it

blocks.note: L is an abbreviation for lecturer

explanation.surface: A cheerful lecturer whose repeated mannerism becomes obvious is behaving lewdly.
explanation.walkthrough: CHEERY has two Es; moving one to the front gives ECHERY.
explanation.definitionFit: Lechery is excessive or offensive sexual desire, so it is a kind of lewdness.

clue.text: 1D election mostly gripping America, regarding POTUS and FLOTUS?

indicators.note: mostly means not all of it, so the final letter of the election word is dropped
gripping means holding tightly within, so the shortened word surrounds the country

blocks.note: 1 Down is SMALL, whose abbreviation is S

explanation.surface: A minor American vote touches on the President and First Lady.
explanation.walkthrough: POLL loses its last L to give POL, which grips USA. POTUS and FLOTUS are the President and First Lady of the United States.
explanation.definitionFit: The President and First Lady are husband and wife, so anything about them as a pair concerns marriage partners.

clue.text: Face piece of film, not quiet, very loud

indicators.note: not here means without, so the letter for quiet is taken out of the film word

blocks.note: piano, the musical direction for soft

explanation.surface: A film excerpt in which a face goes from silent to deafening.
explanation.definitionFit: A cliff face is a steep rock wall; climbers call such a steep surface a face.

clue.text: Cake decorator brought in ice-cream for guide

indicators.note: brought in means placed inside, so the decorator goes into the dessert word

explanation.surface: A cake decorator has been called in to help with the ice-cream.
explanation.definitionFit: A cicerone is a guide who shows sightseers around, named after the eloquent Roman orator Cicero.

clue.text: Following Asian primate to test expertise in plants

blocks.note: abbreviation, as in p. and f.

explanation.surface: A monkey follows to test its botanical knowledge.
explanation.definitionFit: Floristry is the art of arranging flowers, a skill with cut plants.

clue.text: Mystic line leading to district with two trees

blocks.note: a ley line is a supposed alignment of ancient sites

explanation.surface: A ley line runs into a district marked by a pair of trees.
explanation.walkthrough: Leyland cypresses are the fast-growing hedging conifers that cause many British neighbour disputes.
explanation.definitionFit: Leylandii is the plural of the Leyland cypress, a fast-growing hybrid conifer used in hedges.

clue.text: Oil in USA distributed by American state there

indicators.note: distributed means spread around, so the letters are dealt out in a new order

explanation.surface: Oil is shipped across the States by an American region.
explanation.walkthrough: 'there' refers back to the USA in the clue, so the definition is a state of that country.
explanation.definitionFit: Louisiana is one of the United States, on the Gulf of Mexico, with an important oil industry.

clue.text: Director's dreadful pie chart offering minimal layout

indicators.note: dreadful means awful or badly made, suggesting the letters are mangled into a new order

explanation.surface: A director's poor graphic suggests the budget was tiny.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Layout' is used in the sense of outlay, the money laid out.
explanation.definitionFit: Dirt cheap means extremely inexpensive, so buying it requires very little money spent.

clue.text: Arrive to restrain exhibitionist erasing last of the calm

indicators.note: to restrain is to hold in, so the arrival word holds the shortened show-off word
erasing means rubbing out, so a letter disappears from the exhibitionist
'last of' keeps only the last letter of 'the'

explanation.surface: Turning up to rein in a show-off who has lost his cool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Last of the' points to the final letter of the word 'the', which is removed from the exhibitionist.
explanation.definitionFit: Composure is a settled, collected state of mind, as calm is.

clue.text: Badger runs and runs into grass

indicators.note: going into something means ending up inside it, so the paired letters sit in the grass word

blocks.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs, twice

explanation.surface: A badger repeatedly dashes into the long grass.
explanation.definitionFit: To badger and to harry both mean to pester or harass someone persistently.

clue.text: Stays behind regarding water supply

explanation.surface: Someone holds back to discuss the plumbing.
explanation.definitionFit: To remain is to stay on after others go, so 'remains' is the third-person verb for staying behind.

clue.text: Shift millions before deliveries curtailed

indicators.note: curtailed means having its tail cut off, so the final letter of the deliveries word goes

blocks.note: in cricket an over is a set of six deliveries

explanation.surface: Millions are moved ahead of a cut in delivery services.
explanation.walkthrough: An over is a set of six balls bowled in cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: To shift something is to change its position, which is what moving it does.

clue.text: Uproar about performance overturning working-class symbol

indicators.note: overturning means turning over, so the performance word is read backwards
about means around, so the uproar word goes round the turned piece

explanation.surface: A noisy row erupts over a show that subverts a class emblem.
explanation.walkthrough: A flat cap is the cloth cap stereotypically worn by working men in northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: The flat cap is a traditional emblem of the British working man, so it stands for that class.

clue.text: Supports putting restrictions on large navy

indicators.note: restricting something means hemming it in, so the supports surround the size abbreviation

explanation.surface: Allies constraining a big naval force.
explanation.definitionFit: A fleet is a body of warships, and a country's whole navy is often called its fleet.

clue.text: Christmas symbol offering no initial passion

indicators.note: no initial means without its first letter, so the opening of the Christmas word is dropped

explanation.surface: A festive emblem stirring no early enthusiasm.
explanation.definitionFit: Anger is a strong emotion, and passion can mean a fit of rage, as in 'flew into a passion'.

clue.text: Snap after receiving a new scare

indicators.note: receiving means taking in, so the photo word takes in the other two letters

explanation.surface: Someone snaps after getting a fresh fright.
explanation.definitionFit: A panic is a sudden fear or alarm, like a scare.

clue.text: Never corrupt a neophyte

blocks.note: no as an emphatic refusal, never
to vitiate is to spoil or corrupt

explanation.surface: Advice not to lead a newcomer astray.
explanation.definitionFit: A novitiate is a novice in a religious order, and more broadly any beginner or newcomer.

clue.text: Information that's gathered about eco-politician

indicators.note: gathered about means collected around, so the information word encloses the other

blocks.note: gen is British slang for information

explanation.surface: Intelligence gathered on an environmentalist MP.
explanation.definitionFit: A Green is a member of a party campaigning on ecological issues, an environmental politician.

clue.text: Given to wolfing, as it were, chewed up chicory plant

definitions.text: Given to wolfing, as it were

indicators.note: something chewed up is mangled, so these letters come out jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone greedy enough to wolf down a mangled chicory plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wolfing' suggests eating greedily, but here it means turning into a wolf.
explanation.definitionFit: Lycanthropy is the transformation of a human into a wolf, so a lycanthropic person is inclined to become one.
